name: Lee Hsien Loong
_note: Calibration benchmark, not a competitor. Scored on the identical instrument. M1 dry-run subject: data on file, below ranking validity (peer set < 3) so no composite or rank is published. Layer B (Editorial Panel) added 2026-06-01 as a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators: Singapore's Government Effectiveness percentile rank was 100 in 2023, the maximum on the index, with Rule of Law and Control of Corruption also in the top decile. Government effectiveness sits squarely within a head of government's remit, so this is in-domain for C2.

citation.title: Worldwide Governance Indicators — Government Effectiveness, Percentile Rank (GE.PER.RNK), Singapore, data year 2023

metrics.justification: As PAP Secretary-General the leader headed a single party holding a parliamentary supermajority (83 of the 93 elected seats after the 2020 general election). A lone majority party is the pivot in every coalition ordering, so its Shapley-Shubik power index is 1.0. Pivotality is descriptive structural weight, not a merit score.

citation.title: 2020 Parliamentary General Election — Declaration of Results

metrics.justification: No personal corruption charge or conviction of record. The 2017 allegations by his siblings over 38 Oxley Road were a family-property dispute aired in Parliament; the government's position, stated on the record, was that there was no basis to the abuse-of-power allegation, and no charge or adverse finding followed. Recorded as the subject's own factual status only.

citation.title: Ministerial Statement by PM Lee Hsien Loong on Alleged Abuse of Power on 38 Oxley Road

metrics.justification: Crisis handling as PM: the 2009 Resilience Package (S$20.5b, incl. Jobs Credit) met the global financial crisis with recovery and drawn reserves repaid by 2011; the 3 Apr 2020 COVID "circuit breaker" was a decisive measure with a measured case-curve effect but a mixed outcome (migrant-dormitory outbreak). Strong overall, one mixed episode (anchor 3).

Championed reforms delivered as promised: the Pioneer Generation Package became operative on its announced timeline (MediSave top-ups from Jul 2014, outpatient subsidies from 1 Sep 2014), and the Workfare Income Supplement (2007) became a durable, repeatedly expanded scheme. Reform enacted and operative as promised (anchor 4).

citation.title: Pioneers to get MediSave Top-Ups from July

metrics.justification: Institutional conduct: the 2009 draw on past reserves was the first operative use of the elected-presidency reserves-protection check, working through that institution; in the 2017 Oxley Road dispute he made a parliamentary ministerial statement (3 Jul 2017), waived the whip, and recused himself, though critics contest the forum. Net institution-respecting (anchor 3).

citation.title: Ministerial Statement by PM Lee Hsien Loong on 'Alleged Abuse of Power on 38 Oxley Road'

metrics.justification: Public candour: at the 3 May 2011 rally he apologised, twice, for named government failures (the Mas Selamat detainee escape, the Orchard Road floods) and pledged to do better. On-record acknowledgement of failures with explanation (anchor 3).

citation.title: Apology cuts both ways, political watchers say

metrics.justification: At the 29 Aug 2021 National Day Rally he announced that Muslim nurses in public healthcare would be permitted to wear the tudung with their uniform from Nov 2021, framed as a calibrated easing to keep religious harmony, a dated de-escalation of a long-standing religious-accommodation flashpoint (anchor 4).
